target_customer: Finance, sales operations and revenue operations teams at mid-market and enterprise companies that pay variable sales commissions
problem: Companies calculate sales commissions in spreadsheets or in costly legacy tools that need consultants, which causes payout errors, disputes and slow plan changes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for commission and incentive compensation management
product_category: Sales performance management / incentive compensation software

founders.name: Mark Schopmeyer
founders.background_notes: Company blog post signed Mark says he was asked to run commissions for a sales team at BrightRoll before starting the company; education not found.

founders.name: Hubert Wong
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO; described by the company blog as a college friend of the other founders. Education not found.

founders.name: Conway Teng
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the company blog and TechCrunch (called co-CEO there). Background not found.

competitors.name: Xactly
competitors.what: Public incentive compensation management software vendor
competitors.traction_then: Listed on NYSE since 2015; agreed to be taken private by Vista Equity Partners in May 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: A flexible calculation engine for arbitrary commission plans plus CRM and HRIS integrations is standard SaaS engineering with some hard modeling parts.

defensibility.rationale: Once plans and payouts run through the system, finance teams rarely switch, but the early product was copyable by well funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were not seen to copy the product; the company grew to a reported 1.25B valuation in 2022 while newer rivals such as Spiff also raised money.

market_need_then: The founders reported spreadsheet commission processing and expensive legacy tools; a 2017 survey cited by VentureBeat found most companies reported commission payout inaccuracies.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain founder story voice in the company blog

brand_strength.rationale: No source showed press about the brand itself; the name is a captivate plus IQ coinage with no sourced story.

outcome_analysis: CaptivateIQ started from a founder's own pain running commissions at BrightRoll, joined YC in Winter 2018 and grew into a unicorn by January 2022 after a Sequoia led Series A in 2020, an Accel led Series B in 2021 and a $100M Series C. It is still private, with unconfirmed reports of layoffs in late 2022, and no acquisition or IPO has been found.
notes: Total raised stated as 164.6M by TechCrunch, about 5.6M above the three rounds recorded, so earlier funding is missing. A 100K pre-seed in Jan 2018 appears only in aggregator snippets and is unverified. Series B size is 46M per TechCrunch and 45M per another VentureBeat snippet. CB Insights lists a Series D in April 2025 that no other source confirms. A Workday Ventures strategic investment was announced Dec 2021 with no amount found. Layoff reports are unconfirmed forum posts.
